CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with past medical history of rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting for her annual exam. She reports good compliance with exercise, walking, and yoga, which has significantly improved her arthritis. She denies any joint pain, stiffness, or flare-ups over the past year. Regarding her atrial fibrillation, she continues to experience palpitations, most recently about a week ago. She has noted that stress triggers palpitations and has attempted meditation and running to manage stress with limited success. An event monitor was performed last month and will be reviewed today. For her reflux, she reports good control with proton pump inhibitor therapy and dietary modifications, including elimination of soda. She has not had a reflux flare-up in over five months. She endorses nasal congestion related to allergies but denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or nausea/vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Endorses palpitations and nasal congestion from allergies. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, gastroesophageal reflux disease.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly, proton pump inhibitor (Protonix 40 mg daily).

ALLERGIES
Not explicitly stated in conversation.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed in visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Exercises regularly including walking and yoga. Owns a dog.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Heart rate well-controlled. Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, regular rate and rhythm. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Right elbow: Edema and erythema noted with tenderness to palpation. Extremities: No lower extremity edema.

RESULTS
Event monitor: Shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses, characterized by episodes of atrial fibrillation with pauses followed by return to normal sinus rhythm. Autoimmune panel: Normal, indicating well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis on current therapy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Well controlled on methotrexate. Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Refill provided. Rheumatology referral as needed.
2. Atrial fibrillation: Paroxysmal with ongoing palpitations. Refer to cardiology for cardiac ablation to maintain normal sinus rhythm.
3. Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Well controlled. Continue proton pump inhibitor (Protonix 40 mg daily) and dietary modifications, avoiding coffee and spicy foods.
